headline: Every box of fruit checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: With your own fruit and fruit from about 40 other growers going through the Ardmona shed, every box needs the right variety, grade and grower code. Here's what a camera check could look like on your packing line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every box is closed square, with the lid on and nothing caught in the flaps. A box that opens on the pallet means bruised fruit and a rejected load.
labelLede: A box of Granny Smith and a box of Pink Lady are easy to tell apart when open, but not once the lid is on and the label is all anyone sees. The camera checks every box carries the right label for the variety and grade inside, straight and intact.
codeLede: The packed date and grower code tie every box back to the orchard it came from. The system reads the printed code on every box and compares it with the grower, variety and date set for the run.
objectLede: Stems, leaves, tray offcuts and loose parts can end up on the line. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before boxes are palletised.

vocab.alert: Four lids not seated in fifteen minutes. Check the lidder.
